extracted.intended_audience: advanced PARI/GP users and computational number theorists using the number-field/bnf/bnr/rnf APIs
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation and usage rules for PARI/GP data structures and functions dealing with number fields, relative extensions, class field theory, and associated algorithms (bnf, bnr, rnf, nf). Explains accepted input formats, semantics of return structures, flags, and important warnings (e.g. GRH dependence, expensive members).

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic number input formats
rubrics_metrics.description: An algebraic number belonging to K = Q[X]/(T) may be given as a t_INT, t_FRAC or t_POL (implicitly modulo T), a t_POLMOD (modulo T), or a t_COL v of dimension N = [K : Q] representing the element in terms of the computed integral basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that a t_VEC will not be recognized. Use t_COL to express elements as sum_i v[i] * nf.zk[i].

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal input formats
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal may be given as (1) an algebraic number (defining a principal ideal), (2) a prime ideal as a 5-component vector (as output by idealprimedec or idealfactor), or (3) a t_MAT square matrix in Hermite Normal Form (HNF) whose columns represent a Z-basis of the ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use idealhnf to convert any ideal to the preferred t_MAT HNF format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended ideal representation
rubrics_metrics.description: An extended ideal is represented as a 2-component vector [I, t], where I is an ideal and t is an algebraic number, representing the ideal (t)I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when using idealred to track principal ideals implicitly. Multiplicative ideal operations (idealmul, idealsqr, idealinv, idealpow, idealred) update the principal part; other functions silently discard the extended part (e.g. idealadd([I,t],[J,u]) -> I+J).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal part factorization (famat) allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'principal part' t in an extended ideal may be represented as a factorization matrix (famat) in terms of number field elements (possibly the empty factorization matrix factor(1) representing 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When t is a factorization matrix, elements stay in factored form which avoids coefficient explosion. Use nffactorback to recover expanded form if needed. Many functions accept famats (for instance ideallog), so expanding huge elements is often unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite abelian group representation (SNF)
rubrics_metrics.description: A finite abelian group G is represented in user-readable form by its Smith Normal Form as [h, d] or [h, d, g] where h is cardinality, (di) are elementary divisors, and (gi) are generators; G = ⊕(Z/diZ)gi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information can also be retrieved as G.no, G.cyc and G.gen. Ensure di satisfy dn | ... | d2 | d1 and product(di) = h.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters on finite abelian groups
rubrics_metrics.description: A character on ⊕(Z/djZ)gj is given by a row vector χ = [a1,...,an] with χ(∏ g_j^{n_j}) = exp(2πi ∑ a_j n_j / d_j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this vector format to specify characters in routines that accept them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup input as HNF matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the group structure on generators gi, a subgroup H should be input as a square matrix in HNF whose columns express generators of H in terms of the gi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determinant of that matrix equals the index (G : H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable priority rule for relative extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: When defining a relative extension L/K, the nf attached to the base field K must be defined by a variable having lower priority than the variable defining the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., use y for base field K and x for the extension L/K to ensure correct behavior (see Section 2.5.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnf structure and rnf.nf
rubrics_metrics.description: rnf denotes a relative number field as output by rnfinit and rnf.nf is the nf attached to the base field K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rnfinit to initialize relative extensions; many routines expect that precise type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative matrix and ideal list semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: A relative matrix is an m×n matrix with entries in K; its m columns represent elements in K^n. An ideal list is a row vector of fractional ideals of the number field nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are building blocks for pseudo-matrices and projective module descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pseudo-matrix representation of ZK-modules
rubrics_metrics.description: A pseudo-matrix is a 2-component row vector (A, I) where A is a relative m×n matrix and I an ideal list of length n; it defines the torsion-free (projective) ZK-module a1 A1 ⊕ ... ⊕ an An.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any projective ZK-module of finite type in K^m can be given by a pseudo-matrix (A, I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral pseudo-matrix and modules with torsion
rubrics_metrics.description: An integral pseudo-matrix w(A, I, J) is a 3-component row vector where A=(a_{i,j}) is m×n, I=(b1,...,bm), J=(a1,...,an) are ideal lists and a_{i,j} ∈ b_i a_j^{-1}, and it defines modules N, P and a ZK-linear map f : N → P with M = P / f(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use integral pseudo-matrices to represent arbitrary ZK-modules with non-trivial torsion in K^m.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pseudo-basis criteria (non-zero coeffs & linear independence)
rubrics_metrics.description: A pair (A, I) is a pseudo-basis of the module it generates if the a_j are non-zero and the columns A_j are K-linearly independent. The size of the pseudo-basis is n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If A is a relative matrix, linear independence means A is square with non-zero determinant; in HNF it is upper triangular with diagonal entries equal to 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinant of a pseudo-basis/pseudo-matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: The determinant of a pseudo-basis (A, I) is the ideal equal to det(A) times the product of the ideals in I. The determinant of a pseudo-matrix is the determinant of any pseudo-basis of the module it generates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to compare modules and for arithmetic on determinants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modulus representation in class field theory (Archimedean part)
rubrics_metrics.description: A modulus (in class field theory) is a divisor supported on non-complex places: in PARI it is either an ordinary ideal I or a pair [I, a] where a is a vector with r1 {0,1}-components corresponding to the infinite (real) places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The i-th component of a corresponds to the real embedding attached to the i-th real root in K.roots; example: [1,[1,1]] is a modulus for a real quadratic field allowing ramification at either real infinite place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Big ideal (bid) structure for (ZK/m)^* computations
rubrics_metrics.description: A bid (big ideal) is produced by idealstar and is a finite abelian group structure plus technical data needed to compute in (ZK/m)^* and to solve discrete log problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bid for arithmetic and discrete log tasks mod a modulus.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnr/bnf input triple forms and accepted variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Ray number fields (bnr) are defined by a triple A,B,C where [A,B,C] may be [bnr], [bnr, subgroup], [bnr, character], [bnf, mod], [bnf, mod, subgroup]; the last two are kept for backward compatibility but new functions may not accept them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bnf must include units unless the modulus is trivial. For subgroups, input as a square matrix expressing subgroup generators on the ray class group's generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subfield defined by subgroup rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding bnr is the subfield of the ray class field modulo f fixed by the given subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bnrinit and bnr* functions to compute invariants of such subfields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function prefix and type ordering (nf ≤ bnf ≤ bnr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions specific to relative extensions, number fields, Buchmann's number fields and Buchmann's number rays share prefixes rnf, nf, bnf, bnr respectively and take as first argument a number field of that precise type output by rnfinit, nfinit, bnfinit, bnrinit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may substitute a larger type for a smaller one (e.g., pass a bnf where an nf is expected), but a function that requires a bnf will not automatically call bnfinit for you and will error instead. The types are ordered nf ≤ bnf ≤ bnr.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use member functions, not direct component access
rubrics_metrics.description: The data types are complicated; never access a component of a bnf/rnf/bnr directly, always use a proper member function to retrieve data (e.g. bnf.clgp, bnf.zk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct access is discouraged because components are technical and may change; member functions also perform needed computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expensive member functions (.codiff, .t2, .zk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Member functions .codiff, .t2 and .zk perform computations and are relatively expensive in large degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move them out of tight loops and store their results in variables if reused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deprecated member functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some member functions (e.g. futu, tufu) are deprecated and still available but should not be used in new scripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on deprecated members; use current member function interfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependence on GRH for many bnf routines
rubrics_metrics.description: By default many bnf routines (class number, class group structure, generators, regulator, fundamental units) return results that are correct only under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bnfcertify to certify results unconditionally. Defaults for technical parameters are chosen so results are correct under GRH since version 2.4.0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical parameters tech = [c1,c2,nrpid] (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: The tech vector contains c1 ≤ c2 (non-negative reals) and nrpid (max number of small-norm relations per ideal). Bi = ci (log |dK|)^2 define factorbase bounds S(Bi); S(B1) is a factorbase to compute tentative Cl(K), S(B2) is used to prove generation under GRH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These parameters are obsolete; default values (c1=c2=0, nrpid=4) are chosen to be correct under GRH. Setting nrpid between 4 and 20 is reasonable; set to 0 to disable small-norm relations. The algorithm will increase Bi as needed to satisfy the GRH-based proof criterion (Belabas-Diaz-Friedman check).

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning about GRH and need for bnfcertify
rubrics_metrics.description: Results computed from a bnf that has not been certified may be wrong despite appearing consistent; the only unconditional guarantee without bnfcertify is that the computed units generate a subgroup of finite index in the full unit group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run bnfcertify to remove the GRH assumption and obtain a result equal to 1 on success; bnfcertify may require units to be present in the bnf unless flag=1 (which certifies only that the computed class group surjects onto the true class group).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfcertify usage and flag semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfcertify(bnf,{flag=0}) checks whether the bnf results are correct (i.e., can remove GRH). Returns 1 if correct. If flag is present (flag=1) only certify that the class group is a quotient of the computed one; units may form a subgroup and so are not needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: bnfcertify will error if fundamental units are missing unless flag=1. Increase debug level to monitor progress. Library syntax: long bnfcertify0(GEN bnf,long flag) and GEN bnfcertify(GEN bnf).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfcompress produces sbnf (storage-only compressed bnf)
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfcompress(bnf) computes an sbnf (small Buchmann's number field), a 12-component compressed vector containing enough information to rapidly recover a full bnf but which is much smaller for storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An sbnf is useless for most computations and must be converted back to a full bnf before use (bnfinit on sbnf). Components are exact except for roots in v[5]. Do not pass sbnf to routines expecting real bnf/nf objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfinit flag semantics and precision cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfinit(P,{flag=0},{tech=[]}) initializes a bnf. By default results are conditional on GRH. If flag=1, insist on finding fundamental units exactly (may be very slow or fail if units are too large).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If precision is insufficient, gp does not try to compute units by default (flag=0). The tech parameter is obsolete; leave it alone unless debugging/tuning advanced C-level parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnf internal component layout and 'do not access directly'
rubrics_metrics.description: The bnf vector has many technical components (bnf[1]=W relations matrix, bnf[2]=B matrix, bnf[3]=complex logarithmic embeddings of units, ..., bnf[7]=nf, bnf[8]=classgroup+reg+units, bnf[9]=auxiliary data, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These components are technical and rarely used by casual users; always use member functions (bnf.clgp, bnf.reg, bnf.zk, etc.) rather than indexing into bnf directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfisintnorm and bnfisnorm correctness and GRH note
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfisintnorm(bnf,x) computes all solutions (modulo units of positive norm) of Norm(a)=x where a is an integer in bnf. bnfisnorm(bnf,x,{flag=1}) tries to detect whether rational x is a norm in bnf and returns [a,b] with x = Norm(a) * b, searching for S-unit solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If bnf is not certified, correctness depends on GRH. For Galois bnf set flag=0 (then x is a norm iff b=1). The S used must contain primes dividing x; further guarantees when S contains primes < 12 log(disc(Bnf))^2 (Bnf is Galois closure).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfisprincipal solves discrete log in class group and returns [e,t]
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfisprincipal(bnf,x,{flag=1}) tests whether ideal x is principal and returns [e,t] where e are exponents (0 ≤ e_i < d_i) giving the class group discrete log and t is an element with x = (t)∏ g_i^{e_i}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: x is principal iff e is zero vector. The empty vector is used when class number is 1. Flag binary digits: bit 1 — include t in output (else only e); bit 2 — if t cannot be recovered at current precision set t to [] and warn (may require recomputing with higher precision). Prefer symbolic flags nf_GEN (include generators) and nf_FORCE (insist on finding generators) to numeric flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfissunit / bnfsunit / bnfisunit semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfsunit(bnf,S) computes fundamental S-units and returns a 6-component vector v with v[1] minimal generators modulo units, v[2] technical data, v[4] S-regulator, v[5] S-class group structure, v[6] copy of S. bnfissunit(bnf,sfu,x) gives exponents of x on fundamental S-units and roots of unity; bnfisunit(bnf,x) decomposes a unit x on fundamental units and roots of unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If bnf lacks explicit fundamental units due to low precision, bnfisunit may still return exponents relative to implicitly stored units. Use appropriate routines and increase precision/flag to compute explicit units if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnflog / bnflogdegree / bnflogef outputs and finiteness condition
rubrics_metrics.description: bnflog(bnf,l) returns data on the l-logarithmic class group ClF (if the group is finite). bnflogdegree(nf,A,l) returns the exponential of the l-adic logarithmic degree deg_F A. bnflogef(nf,pr) returns logarithmic ramification and residue degrees [˜e,˜f] for a prime pr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: bnflog returns only if the logarithmic class group is finite (otherwise it may loop). Use idealprimedec to obtain pr for bnflogef.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfnarrow computes narrow class group format
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfnarrow(bnf) computes the narrow class group and returns a 3-component row vector v analogous to bnf.clgp: v.no (narrow class number), v.cyc (cyclic SNF components), v.gen (generators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: bnf need not contain fundamental units for bnfnarrow; this function is a special case of bnrinit.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnfsignunit and totally positive units extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: bnfsignunit(bnf) computes an r1 × (r1 + r2 − 1) ±1 matrix giving signs of real embeddings of fundamental units. Helper functions tpuexpo and tpu use this to compute exponents and totally positive fundamental units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: tpuexpo returns exponent matrix for totally positive generators; tpu constructs totally positive fundamental units via nffactorback and bnf.tufu.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrL1 computes L-values at s=0 or s=1 with flags
rubrics_metrics.description: bnrL1(bnr,{H},{flag=0}) returns, for each character χ of the ray class group trivial on H, the value at s=1 (or s=0) of the abelian L-function attached to χ. For s=0 it returns [r_χ,c_χ] such that L(s,χ)=c s^{r}+O(s^{r+1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag binary digits: bit 1 unset -> compute at s=0, set -> compute at s=1; bit 2 unset -> primitive L-function, set -> remove Euler factors at primes dividing modulus; bit 3 -> also return the character. This function can fail with 'overflow in zeta_get_N0' if discriminant too large for the approximate functional equation.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrchar returns characters satisfying constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: bnrchar(bnr,g,{v}) returns all characters χ on bnr.clgp such that χ(g_i) = e(v_i). If v omitted returns characters trivial on g. g and v must have same length, with v_i rational whose denominator divides order of g_i. g may be replaced by a matrix of discrete logs to specify a subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to enumerate characters trivial on a subgroup or with prescribed values; output is vectors of exponents describing characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrclassno and bnrclassnolist for ray class numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: bnrclassno(A,{B},{C}) returns relative degree [L:K] for a class field defined by A,B,C (various allowed forms); if A is a bnf and B a modulus returns the ray class number. bnrclassnolist(bnf,list) returns class numbers for a list of moduli.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: bnrclassno is faster than bnrinit when only class number is desired. bnrclassnolist expects list from ideallist or ideallistarch and returns corresponding class numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrconductor flag semantics and accepted inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: bnrconductor(A,{B},{C},{flag=0}) returns the conductor f of the subfield defined by [A,B,C]. If flag=0 returns f; flag=1 returns [f, Clf, H] (Clf = ray class group modulo f, H subgroup); flag=2 returns [f, bnr(f), H] (bnr(f) without generators unless input had them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of subgroup H one may pass a character χ; in that case the function returns the conductor of Ker(χ) or also χ expressed on the minimal ray class group depending on flag. Use bnrconductor over obsolete bnrconductorofchar.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrdisc flag bits meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: bnrdisc(A,{B},{C},{flag=0}) returns discriminant/signature data [N,r1,D] for class field L over K depending on flag bits: bit 1 unset -> absolute data relative to L/Q (N=[L:Q], r1=#real places of L, D discriminant of L/Q); bit 1 set -> relative data for L/K (N=[L:K], r1=#real places of K unramified in L, D relative discriminant ideal). Bit 2 set -> if the modulus is not the conductor of L, only return 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose flags appropriately to obtain absolute or relative discriminant and signature information.
